previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with a complex medical history including systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, prior ischemic bowel with ileostomy, and coronary artery disease was admitted for dizziness, abdominal pain, fever, and dark stool. She was found to have hypotension likely due to gastrointestinal blood loss and increased ostomy output. Initial labs showed stable but low hemoglobin, and imaging ruled out pancreatitis or bowel ischemia. An upper endoscopy revealed a bleeding gastric polyp, which was banded successfully. She required one unit of packed red blood cells during dialysis due to anemia. Her blood pressure stabilized with IV fluids, and labetalol was held. She improved clinically with resolution of abdominal pain and stabilization of vital signs. She was discharged home with services for ostomy care, medication adjustments including increased pantoprazole and addition of loperamide, and plans for outpatient follow-up with gastroenterology, cardiology, and primary care.

Dear Ms. ___-

came to the emergency room because of increasing pain and 
swelling in your left knee and shoulder.

Lugdunesis. The orthopedic surgeons took you to the operating
